rationale: 17 scalp-intent trades to 2026-08-18 showed winners' MAE median -2.6 pips (worst -8.8 excluding one 92-hour hold) while the two losers ran to -40.7 and -33.5. A stop halves dispersion without cutting winners. The 10-pip value was CHOSEN BY SCANNING THOSE 17 TRADES, so those trades are fitting data and are excluded from the evidence set. This registration freezes the rule before new data.

population.definition: manual trades whose take-profit distance at entry is <= 15.0 pips
population.note: classification uses TP distance at entry, never realised hold time; classifying by hold time makes winners close fast and losers migrate out, producing a fake 100% win rate

rule.note: a trade opened without a broker stop, or above the margin fraction, is recorded as a DISCIPLINE VIOLATION and excluded from the evidence set - it is not silently dropped

measurement.unit_rationale: trade sizes in the prior sample ranged 1,000-35,000 units, a 35x spread; measuring in JPY would measure position size rather than method
measurement.statistic: one-sided 95% lower bound on mean pips per trade

required_n_rationale: the fitted estimate implies 21 trades, but the stop distance was fitted on the same sample. Assuming the true edge shrinks to ~70% of the fitted value (mu 1.62, sd 6.45) gives n = 43. Registered at 45.

decision_criteria.reject: lower bound <= 0 with >= 90 clean trades, or mean <= 0 at any point beyond 45
decision_criteria.abort: any single trade loses more than 25 pips (means the stop is not being honoured)

forbidden: changing stop_distance_pips, take_profit_max_pips, max_margin_used_fraction or required_n after the first clean trade is recorded
excluding a losing trade as 'not really a scalp'
reporting the prior 17 trades as evidence
computing a win rate or mean over any subset chosen after seeing outcomes
